answer: One agent, one clean record: a licensed screening agency runs a fresh criminal-record check on the operator, then signs a challenge binding the agent key to that single verified record, and the relic of the check is re-run against the public court index every epoch. A second key claiming the same record is rejected outright, since the agency holds the file. Forging 1,000 identities needs 1,000 clean records at roughly $75 each, about $75,000 — a timber of cost no script can fake, and any record can be revoked on fraud, a river an attacker cannot dodge.
